objectives: Blend initial /y/, a short vowel, and a final consonant to decode taught CVC words.
Decode yak, yam, yap, yes, yet, and yen without relying on pictures.
Track each grapheme from left to right and check the final consonant.
Distinguish /y/ from similar initial sounds while preserving the vowel and ending.
concepts: A CVC word has a consonant, vowel, and consonant sequence.
The initial grapheme y represents /y/ in these taught words.
Left-to-right blending combines each sound in order.
The final consonant distinguishes words such as yak, yam, and yap.

definitions.definition: A word with a consonant sound, a short vowel sound, and a final consonant sound.
To combine individual speech sounds in order to read a word.
A letter or letter group representing a speech sound.

workedExamples.solution: Say /y/, /a/, /m/; blend the sounds to read yam.
Both begin /y/ and contain short /a/; the final /k/ or /p/ changes the word.
Say /y/, /e/, /t/ in order, then blend yet.

commonMistakes: Guessing from a picture before blending the letters.
Changing the short vowel while blending.
Ignoring the final consonant and reading yak as yap.
keyTakeaways: Point to each grapheme from left to right.
Say the final consonant before blending the whole word.
Check that the blended word matches every letter.

basic.prompt: Choose the word that begins /y/ and ends /k/.

conceptual.prompt: Read y-e-t by blending the sounds in order.

application.prompt: Compare yak and yap; identify the sound that changes.
application.answer: The final sound changes from /k/ to /p/.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Decode a fresh card by pointing to each grapheme before blending.
higherOrderThinking.answer: Blend the initial consonant, vowel, and final consonant in order.

mixedReview.prompt: Read one target word, identify its initial sound, vowel, and final sound, then explain how the sounds make the word.
mixedReview.answer: Name and blend the three phonemes in order.

mistakeBasedRevision: Guessing from a picture before blending the letters.
Changing the short vowel while blending.
Ignoring the final consonant and reading yak as yap.
weakTopicRevision: If decoding accuracy is below target, isolate the weak phoneme or reading step, model it, practise with guided examples, then reassess with fresh words.

activities.name: Sound-box blending
steps: Place one counter in each of three boxes.
Say the sound for y, the vowel, and the final consonant.
Sweep a finger under all three boxes and blend the word.
Repeat with yak, yam, yap, yes, yet, and yen.

activities.name: Final-sound contrast
steps: Hold the initial /y/ and short /a/ steady.
Explain how the final consonant changes the word.

outcomes: Decode at least 8 of 10 taught y-initial CVC words by sound blending.
Identify the initial, medial-vowel, and final sounds in a CVC word.
Self-correct a misread word by checking every grapheme.

questions.question: Which word begins with /y/ and ends with /k/?
Which word starts with /y/ and ends with /t/?
Which word does NOT begin with /y/?
Which word has the same final sound as yak?
Why should a learner point to letters from left to right?
options: To blend each sound in order
To read only the last sound

questions.question: A learner reads yak as yap. What needs checking?

answerKeys.explanation: Yak begins with /y/ and ends with /k/.
The ordered sounds blend to form yam.
Yes contains initial /y/, short /e/, and final /s/.
Yet starts with /y/ and ends with /t/.
Pack and yak both end with /k/.
The sequence y-e-n blends to yen.
Left-to-right tracking preserves the order of the phonemes.
Yak and yap differ in their final consonant.
